extracted.intended_audience: students/apprentices and practical users of arithmetic (merchants, teachers)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and pedagogical guidance from an early-modern Italian arithmetic treatise covering congruent numbers, methods to form squares, extraction of square and cube roots (arithmetically and geometrically), fraction representation and manipulation, and teaching practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeri congrui (finding congruent numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to find numbers 'congrui' (congruent), by choosing integers and combining their squares/operations to produce numbers congruent to a given one. Original wording: "£ voi trouare numericongrui fa'cofi poni.2 .numeri acafo interi ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithmic steps and examples are given (take two integers, compute their related square-forms, double/duplicate and add to obtain congruent numbers). Example mentions: 'Il primo fa.9.ri fecondo.64 insieme fanno.75' and operations like duplicating first and second number, multiplying and adding to obtain numbers declared 'congrui'. The text lists many explicit resulting numbers (a long sequence of derived values), illustrating the iterative production of congruent numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing many square numbers by arranged squares
rubrics_metrics.description: Method of arranging successive square numbers in a table/figure so that adding particular squares to existing congruent numbers yields further square numbers. Original phrasing: 'ponere vna tauola oe numeri quadratitcioc ... per numeri congrui ... femp2e hano...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place squares orderly in a figure and proceed 'mano in mano' adding the squares of certain indices to obtain new square numbers; the treatise gives sequences and examples demonstrating how to continue the process 'fine a.1.' to produce arbitrarily many square numbers congruent in the desired way. Several explicit numeric examples and a long tabulation are provided in the text to illustrate the method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraction of square roots via geometric/arrangement methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometric approach to extract square roots by constructing squares/rectangles, drawing perpendiculars and diameters, and using intersections to determine the length corresponding to the root. E.g.: 'vn quadrilatero ... trovare vna linea ... la linea in linea recta nel ponto ... la linea compoita ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include forming a quadrilateral or square of given proportions, drawing perpendiculars/diameters and using intersection points to identify the side whose length corresponds to the square root. The text emphasizes construction with straightedge-like operations (perpendiculars, diameters, joining intersections) as an instrument-based method for obtaining roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetical extraction of cube roots using the 'triplati' method
rubrics_metrics.description: A stepwise arithmetic algorithm for cube-root extraction based on generating 'triplati' (triples) and 'fubtriplati' (subtriples), arranging them in figures/tables, multiplying and iterating to obtain successive digits of the cube root. Original phrasing: 'De trtractione ... Delle radici cubete ... come trouare la... cuba ... come si fa ... triplati ... fubtriplati ... metti qud p2Ìmotnplafoclx banali e fa dx ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: generate lists of tripled values for candidate digits, place them in a table (keeping tripli and subtripli distinct), multiply the candidate digit by the appropriate triple/subtriple sets, subtract and iterate; find successive digits by choosing those whose multiples bring the cubic closest without exceeding. The chapter gives worked examples and explicit numeric demonstrations (mentions of large illustrative numbers like sequences of 9s, usage of multiplying by 3,7,9 etc) and instructs repeating the process 'allo fine' to refine the cube root digit-by-digit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric cube-root extraction using constructions (quadrilaterals and diameters)
rubrics_metrics.description: A geometric instrument method to extract cube roots: construct a quadrilateral with one side proportional to the given number, draw diagonals/diameters and certain perpendiculars/intersections to produce a segment equal to the cube root. Original phrasing: 'De in vamone... per inllrumenta gometericrar ... fa^rai vn quadrilatero ... tira la .SapommUTa ... tira la linea ... tangente el canto ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a rectangle/quadrilateral of specified length and width; draw diagonals and diameters 'dentro a qudlo quadrilatero', mark intersections and use measured segments from those constructions as the cube root. The text gives a geometric sequence of operations (draw from point to point, form tangents, use centers and intersections) as an alternative to the arithmetical algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and denomination of fractions (notation and naming parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard way to represent fractions: a full integer split into parts, denoted by a numerator and denominator separated by a line, and named by denominations (terzo, quarto, quinto, etc.). Original wording: 'De t(ilfintrione ... Ètto € vna o vero piu parti ve vno itegro ... vna riga fraloro ... Denoiato2e:vd vnuo oicitur numcrato2 ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that a fraction is 'una o più parti' of an integer; the notation uses a line ('la riga') with the part above and the denomination below; the denomination names the division (terzo = 1/3, quarto = 1/4, etc.). The chapter describes how to interpret these parts and how the size of a part relates to the denominator (more parts → smaller unit), giving guidance for naming and reading fractions in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic operations on fractions (multiplication, division, copying rows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for manipulating fractions via multiplying numerators/denominators and using 'copie' (copying rows) to compute results; includes instructions for forming intermediary rows and multiplying across to effect operations. Original phrasing: 'ponerce Copia u vna riga c! partirox ... Dieo d?epiima diebi qiidio Difopia la riga:doc ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To perform operations one may copy the line (row) of parts, form another row for the operation, multiply corresponding items as prescribed, and then reassemble or reduce. The text gives explicit step sequences showing use of duplicated rows and multiplying across to obtain the fractional product or quotient, and indicates how to add syllabic/decimal adjuncts when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding common divisors and reducing fractions (partitore comune)
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques to find a common divisor ('partitore comune') for reducing fractions and simplifying computations, by trial division and progressive factoring using small primes and other methods. Original text: 'trovare Detto fd?ifatore ... molti modi ... per molti libri ... cercàdo ... metàdo pii nneri avno a vno cóen^àdo ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise recommends trying successive divisors (2,3,5,7, etc.), using multiple methods recorded in other books, and persisting until the fraction is simplified. It notes that sometimes a number will not be divisible by small primes and thus one should continue searching higher factors; several pragmatic heuristics and examples are cited for obtaining the greatest common divisor in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominational partitions and proportional splitting (fractional denominations and conversions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and examples for partitioning an integer into denominational parts (e.g., halves, thirds, quarters), expressing composite parts (e.g., 'tre quarti'), and how to convert or remark denominational relationships. The text discusses how to name and work with complex partitions and how a 'parte' relates to the unit. Original phrasing: 'la parte fia meno2e od tutto quello per fee manifdlo ... ... la parte fia vna vnita ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to express compound fractions (e.g., 3/4) in terms of units and parts, and how to treat partitions when performing operations (e.g., splitting into 2,4,5 parts yields denominational names). Includes examples showing stepwise partitioning (per 2, per 3, per 4) and guidance for when parts are further subdivided; recommended procedures for recording and combining these partitions when doing calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical best practices for teaching and learning arithmetic
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on instruction and practice: frequent, varied practice, patient repetitive exercise, not beating or over-punishing learners, and using multiple methods until the student attains skill. Original snippets: '... al piaticbo ofxrare oe ariti?/mefica ballante ... per la igno2anria odfi molti ... non cognofere abtìbgni dx parte ...' and later pedagogical remarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author recommends many short repetitions, trying different (easier and more laborious) methods until the pupil sees what fits, pausing and letting operations settle in memory, and warns against harshness. Specific counsel: practice until mastery ('non predericoma... prima non prona'), try both laborious and quicker methods, give pupils varied exposures and allow time for internalization.
